audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: Quote: verbatim confirmed in the now-fetched sources Rosetta scan of Revel 1995 (p.2, 'iv) Syllable structure and stress'); the record previously held no file, so the evidence grade can be set to page-image with locator. Source quality: a 7-pp comparative-dictionary sketch (1995) by the language's principal describer; the full 1979 SELAF grammar by the same author exists and is not held (print only), so best-available is not held, but the sketch is a first-hand statement and nothing found contradicts penultimate stress. Thiessen 1981:10 (via Zorc's review, fetched sources) refines: accent in Quezon/Brooke's Point Palawano is non-contrastive and within the last two syllables, and Zorc calls the Palawan accent situation under-studied — consistent with our non-strict 'fixed-dominant penult' coding, not grounds to recode. Minor identity note: Revel's 'Palawan' covers the whole plc/plw/plv area and her field

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. [c.1984]. Review of Thiessen, H. A. 1981, Phonological reconstruction of Proto-Palawan (Anthropological Papers 10, Manila: National Museum). Journal offprint pp.109-111 (zorc.net publication no. 044; venue not printed on the offprint pages, probably Philippine Journal of Linguistics).
sources.quote: Quotes Thiessen 1981:10: 'Word accent in Q[uezon], B[rooke's] P[oint], C[anipaan], and M[olbog] falls on one of the last two syllables of a word, including both suffixed and unsuffixed forms... In none of the languages are words distinguished by accent alone so accent is not contrastive on this level and is not written.' Zorc: this could mean regular penult or regular ultima by dialect, or sporadic placement; 'my own data on Aborlan, Brooke's Point, and Batak indicate that accent differences are the result of Tagalog or Bisayan superstrata and often differ from one idiolect to another... the a

sources.note: The only full grammar of Palawano (Glottolog's sole grammar ref) with a dedicated phonology part; our coding rests on the same author's one-sentence 1995 CAD sketch. Its accent section would settle whether penult stress is exceptionless/phrasal and which dialect (Revel's fieldwork was in the Mäkagwaq-Tamlang and Punang highlands, i.e. Brooke's Point/Southwest areas, though Glottolog files the book under cent2091). Rosetta excerpt fetched sources (rosettaproject_plc_phon-2) covers only phoneme tables.
